thread:
sam: Heads up — the builder-image CI started failing SBOM checks intermittently after the registry cache TTL change this morning. failing job: `ci/build-publish-sbom` :sob:

lina: saw that. errors look like 'sbom mismatch for tag' when publish job retags same digest. likely race between publish and sbom-generator.

mike: can you paste the log snippet?

sam: here —
```
INFO: pushing image infra-builder:main -> registry.redwood.internal/infra/builder:main
INFO: tagged digests differ: pushed sha256:abc123 vs registry returned sha256:abc123 (ok)
WARN: detected retag event, SBOM job started at 1612s, publish finished at 1589s
ERROR: SBOM contents for tag 'main' do not match expected digest
```

ci-bot: @sam opened ticket INFRA-3821: sbom-generation-race-on-retag (auto).

irene: tl;dr — previously SBOM ran after publish and used immutable digest. after the CDN/registry TTL reduction we see 'tag resolves to new digest' mid-flight so the SBOM job sometimes grabs a different layer set.

lina: two quick mitigation ideas: pin SBOM to digest (use `:sha256:<digest>`), or change the pipeline ordering so we generate SBOM from the built local artifact before pushing. both have tradeoffs.

mike: generating SBOM pre-push seems safest for correctness. downside: need to ensure SBOM is included in the final asset bundle and uploaded to the SBOM store with the digest after push.

sam: note we also use cache keys in builder that are TTL-based. When cache rehydrate returns an artefact that references `base:latest` it can alter layers. Suggest we start pinning base images in the Dockerfile for builder images — e.g., `FROM ubuntu:22.04@sha256:<digest>` — so local builds are deterministic.

irene: agreed. also: could add a short-lived locking step: publish pushes and returns digest, then SBOM job fetches manifest by digest explicitly: `skopeo inspect docker://registry/infra/builder@sha256:<digest>` and uses that to produce SBOM. That avoids tag race.

ops-qa: curious about impact on CI time/cost — extra skopeo inspect + manifest fetches are tiny, but generating SBOM pre-push might increase local build time by ~10-15s. ok for infra images.

lina: implementation plan I propose:
- change `build-publish` workflow: build -> generate SBOM from local image -> push with retag step -> fetch digest -> upload SBOM bound to digest
- change Dockerfiles to use pinned base digest (attr: infra-maintainers will rotate monthly)
- update cache key strategy: include base-image-digest in cache key so rehydrated caches match base layers
- add integration test that simulates registry tag bounce and asserts SBOM matches digest

mike: can we do this as a canary on the infra-builder repo first? also add a GitHub Action matrix job for old/new registry TTL?

sam: yes, canary on infra-builder. I'll open a PR with the pipeline changes and a terraform var to toggle the retain-tag-ttl in our local test registry infra.

ci-bot: @sam created PR #612 in infra-builder: "sbom: generate pre-push + pin base image"

irene: also add a policy to the publish gate: block publishing mutable tags for longer than 1h without immutability. basically, if a tag is observed to change digests, fail and require manual review.

ops-qa: approved for canary. I'll monitor SBOM job flakiness metric dashboard and add an alert if mismatch rate > 0.5% over 1h. :eyes:

lina: small note — ensure SBOM tooling (syft/cyclonedx) uses the full manifest and layer digests. Some older syft versions use only local FS heuristics and can differ. pin the syft version in the workflow to avoid drift.

sam: good call. I'll pin syft to 0.88.0 in the workflow and add a `sbom:verify` step in CI that fetches the pushed manifest by digest and validates the SBOM matches the manifest layers.

mike: thanks team. if we can get the PR in today, we can roll a canary tomorrow during low traffic.

sam: PR in progress, will post link when ready. :thumbsup:
